planting.note: Start seed indoors 8-12 weeks before the last frost since this slow-starting species needs a long season to reach flowering size, and set transplants out only once night temperatures stay reliably above 50 degrees F.

directions: This Australian native in the bellflower family forms a tidy, freely branching mound of thread-fine, finely cut foliage, covered from early summer through frost with five-pointed, star-shaped flowers in sky blue, lilac-blue, or white depending on the selection. It is still widely sold in the seed trade under its older names Laurentia and Solenopsis axillaris even though current botanical treatments place it in Isotoma, and is distinct from the low creeping groundcover Isotoma fluviatilis already in this database. Hardy as a perennial only in zones 9-11, it is grown as a warm-season bedding and container annual everywhere else, prized for edging, hanging baskets, and mixed containers. The milky sap is a known skin and eye irritant, so wear gloves when pinching back or deadheading spent flowers.
sources: University of Arkansas Division of Agriculture — Plant of the Week
